proposal.hypothesis: Li8SiO6 is a very Li-rich orthosilicate, a wide-gap oxide with Si4+, which is hard to reduce. Its high Li2O content, like Li3BO3, should limit anion exchange and S/P release with Li6PS5Cl, unlike the phosphate, fluoride and chloride contacts. The silicate family has not been tested yet.
proposal.motivation: Li3BO3 (mp-aaaabojb) was the best so far (penalty 0.189, bin 9), showing that Li-rich oxyanion frameworks limit interfacial reactions. Li2O (bin 18) and the Li-rich borate analogues (bins 90 and 36) show that the cation and anion details matter, so a Li-rich silicate is a new test of this trend.

proposal.hypothesis: Li8ZrO6 is a very Li2O-rich oxide with Zr4+, which is hard to reduce. Like Li8SiO6 (bin 9) and Li3BO3 (bin 9), its high Li content and oxyanion framework should limit anion exchange and S/P release with Li6PS5Cl. Zr4+ may give a different contact chemistry from Si4+ or B3+, and this tests whether an oxide-rich zirconate can go below the bin-9 penalty.
proposal.motivation: Li8SiO6 (mp-aaaabqgb) and Li3BO3 (mp-aaaabojb) were the lowest-penalty results so far (about 0.189 eV/non-Li atom, bin 9). Li-rich oxyanion frameworks consistently did better than the phosphate, fluoride and chloride coatings (bins 15-16), so a Li-rich zirconate tests the same trend with a different metal.

proposal.hypothesis: Li6Si2O7 is a Li-rich silicate, close to the Li8SiO6 chemistry that gave the lowest penalty so far (bin 9). Its Si4+ oxyanion framework is hard to reduce, and its Li2O content should limit the anion exchange and S/P release seen with the phosphate, fluoride and chloride contacts. It has less Li2O per Si than Li8SiO6, so it tests whether a more network-forming silicate changes the contact penalty.
proposal.motivation: Li8SiO6 (mp-aaaabqgb) gave penalty 0.189 eV/non-Li atom (bin 9), the best non-borate result so far, which suggests Li-rich silicate frameworks suppress sulfide contact reactions.
